user.title: Set up HomeKey Household
user.description:
HomeKey Household can reach a node either through the official MQTT integration (a whole household, push-based, needs a broker) or directly over the node's own HTTPS API (one node, polled, no broker at all).

A node that is already online is discovered automatically — check Settings → Devices & Services for a discovered card first. Continue here to set up the MQTT transport by hand. For the broker-less transport, make sure mDNS works on your network so the node can be discovered; otherwise add it over MQTT.

direct.title: Connect to HomeKey node
direct.description:
Found **{name}** ({model}) at {host}:{port}, firmware {version}.

It will be reached directly over HTTPS, with no broker, using the certificate fingerprint it advertises:

`{expected}`

The node's Web UI shows the same value under Misc → Security. **If the two differ, stop** — nothing else about this connection can be trusted.

Certificate the node presented when last checked: `{presented}`

Enter the credentials of the node's own Web UI (not your Home Assistant ones). The lock is controlled over this same authenticated connection, so these credentials are what protects it.

data_description.username: The user name configured on the node's Web UI (default admin).
data_description.password: The password you set during the node's first-run setup. It is stored in this integration entry, exactly as the official MQTT integration stores a broker password, because the node has to be authenticated on every poll.

reauth_confirm.title: Reauthenticate with the node
reauth_confirm.description:
The node at {host}:{port} no longer accepts the stored credentials. Enter the current Web UI credentials.

The pinned certificate fingerprint is still required to match:

`{expected}`

If the node was replaced or factory reset, its certificate has changed and this form cannot help: remove the integration entry and add it again so the new certificate is confirmed.

mqtt_guide.title: Configure MQTT
mqtt_guide.description:
Install and configure the official MQTT integration, then come back and press Submit.

1. Go to [Settings → Devices & Services](/config/integrations).
2. Click **Add Integration** and choose **MQTT**.
3. Enter your broker host/port (and credentials if required) and finish the wizard.
4. Press **Submit** below to re-check the connection.

The integration is a pure consumer of the firmware MQTT topics; the broker can be Mosquitto or any MQTT broker.

Documentation: {docs}

mqtt_express.title: Configure MQTT automatically
mqtt_express.description:
Enter your broker details. HomeKey Household will create the official MQTT integration entry for you.

Use the MQTT protocol version 5 (the default; the firmware is also compatible with 3.1.1). Host 127.0.0.1 is only correct if the broker runs on the same host as Home Assistant.

mqtt_addon.title: Use the MQTT add-on
mqtt_addon.description:
Install and start the official Mosquitto broker add-on via Supervisor, then wire up the MQTT integration automatically.

This needs no broker details. It is available only on Home Assistant OS or a Supervised installation, because only there can Supervisor install the add-on. Press **Submit** to continue.

household.title: HomeKey Household
household.description:
Configure a HomeKey household. MQTT is reused from the Home Assistant MQTT integration.

All fields below are editable — the values are prefilled from the device/MQTT discovery where possible, but you can change any of them before submitting.

data_description.household_id: Matches the household_id published on the household MQTT topics, e.g. HOME-001.
data_description.recovery_secret: Used only to derive the HMAC command key. Never sent over MQTT and never stored by Home Assistant. Example format: 24359u234fhurbgerbvuiebvubervbvun. Keep a copy in a safe place (e.g. your password manager) — Home Assistant does not keep it, so if you lose it you cannot re-derive the command key.
data_description.salt: The salt the firmware uses when deriving the command key, if one is configured. Leave empty if the firmware uses no salt.
data_description.command_control: When disabled the lock entity is read-only. Commands fail closed without a credential.

error.invalid_household_id: Household ID must be 1-64 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_-].
error.invalid_recovery_secret: The recovery secret must not be empty.
error.mqtt_not_configured: MQTT is still not configured or not connected. Finish the MQTT setup, then try again.
error.mqtt_setup_failed: Could not create the MQTT integration automatically. Please add the MQTT integration manually from Settings → Devices & Services, then try again.
error.cannot_connect: Home Assistant could not reach the MQTT broker at that address. Check the host and port, and make sure the broker is running and reachable from this machine. Note: 127.0.0.1 only works if the broker runs on the same host as Home Assistant.
error.mqtt_addon_failed: Could not install or start the Mosquitto broker add-on. Check Supervisor, then try again or use the express setup instead.
error.mqtt_addon_unavailable: Supervisor did not offer the Mosquitto broker add-on for installation. Install the 'Mosquitto broker' add-on from Settings → Add-ons, start it, then choose this option again — or use the express setup instead.
error.addon_info_failed: Supervisor could not read the Mosquitto broker add-on's information. Open Settings → Add-ons → Mosquitto broker and check that it is installed correctly, then try again.
error.addon_connection_failed: The Mosquitto broker add-on did not come up in time. Open Settings → Add-ons → Mosquitto broker, confirm it is running, then try again. If it keeps failing, check the add-on's own log for errors.
error.addon_start_failed: The Mosquitto broker add-on started, but Home Assistant could not connect to it. Open the add-on's Log tab and fix any startup errors (for example, a port conflict or a broken configuration), then try again. Using the express setup with your own broker credentials also works.
error.node_unreachable: Home Assistant could not reach the node at that address. Check that it is powered on and on the same network, then try again.
error.node_auth_failed: The node rejected those credentials. Enter the username and password for the node's own Web UI (Misc -> Security on the node), not your Home Assistant ones.
error.fingerprint_mismatch: The certificate the node presented is not the one it advertises over mDNS. Do not continue: the device may have been replaced or factory reset, or something on the network may be impersonating it. Compare the two fingerprints above with the value in the node's Web UI (Misc → Security). If the node was legitimately replaced or reset, wait for it to be discovered again and add it from that card.
error.tls_required: The node is not serving HTTPS. Its firmware refuses to send state or configuration in the clear, so there is nothing to connect to yet. Enable HTTPS on the node's Web UI (Misc → Security) and try again.
error.no_household: The node has no household yet. Everything else is working, but a household is what its entities are keyed on (and what makes its credentials meaningful). On the node's Web UI open Provision, issue a one-time code, then join with a household id, and try again.
error.unsupported_protocol: The node speaks a different API protocol version than this integration understands. Update the integration, or update the node's firmware.

abort.not_hassio: The MQTT add-on option is only available on Home Assistant OS or a Supervised installation.
abort.tls_required: The discovered node is not serving HTTPS. Enable HTTPS on the node's Web UI (Misc → Security), then add it again.
abort.no_fingerprint: The discovered node did not advertise a certificate fingerprint, so there is nothing to pin it to. Update the node's firmware, then add it again.
abort.unsupported_protocol: The discovered node speaks API protocol {protocol}; this integration understands {supported}. Update the integration, or update the node's firmware.
abort.node_address_unknown: The node's advertisement did not include a usable address, so there is nothing to connect to. Reboot the node so that it advertises itself again, then discover it once more.
abort.household_already_configured: Household {household_id} is already configured as “{title}”. Its entities are keyed on the household, so adding this node again would create a duplicate set. Remove the existing entry first if you want to switch this household to the broker-less connection.

init.title: HomeKey Household options
init.description: Rotate the command credential or change availability settings. Leaving the recovery secret blank keeps the current key.

data.recovery_secret: Recovery secret (leave blank to keep current key)
data.password: Web UI password (leave blank to keep the current one)
data.backup_include_credentials: Include the node's keys in each backup (it becomes the keys to the door)

data_description.legacy_client_id_prefix: Prefix of the legacy client id (default ESP_). Used only to read the shared broker LWT availability topic.
data_description.salt: The node holds the recovery secret and this salt as bytes and reports both as hex. Both are needed to derive the command key: a secret without the matching salt derives a key the node rejects with bad_mac, and the rejection is not visible from here. The node prints its own salt as recovery_salt on its Household page.
data_description.host: Optional. A backup or a restore travels over the node's own HTTPS API, not over MQTT, so it needs the node's address, its certificate fingerprint and its Web UI credentials. Leave empty and backup or restore will say they cannot reach the node.
data_description.fingerprint: The SHA-256 fingerprint the node reports on its own API page. It is what pins the connection: without it, the integration will not send a credential to whatever answers at that address.
data_description.backup_include_credentials: The backup then also carries the reader credential store - its identity and the enrolled issuers' endpoint keys - and the HomeKit pairing state. That is what lets a replacement node come back without every tag being enrolled again, and it is also what makes the file the keys to the door: keep it where you would keep a key, not in a chat message. Off, each backup is configuration only, and restoring one means the enrolled devices have to be provisioned again. The node reports which kind a copy actually is, and the backup sensor shows that for the newest stored one.

error.invalid_recovery_secret: The recovery secret must not be empty.
